images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of SUPRA-Tex.Left: image-to-material translation.A 2D material translator estimates lighting-separated albedo, metallic, and roughness maps from a single reference image.Middle: native observation encoding.Using the meshℳ\mathcal{M}and camera projectionπ\pi, we project valid predictions onto visible surface voxels and omit unobserved voxels from the partial PBR input. The frozen material encoderEmatE_{\mathrm{mat}}maps these partial PBR attributes into the generation target’s latent space. These latents, together with coverage and boundary metadata, form the observation representation𝒞o\mathcal{C}_{o}.Right: observation-guided completion.Conditioned on geometry latentsGG, the interleaved flow transformer generates complete material latentsZ0Z_{0}from noiseZ1Z_{1}. In the inset, the fixed, read-only streamOOsupplies keys and values, while the generation streamXXalternates updates over cells without observations (𝒰\mathcal{U}) and the full surface (𝒮\mathcal{S}). The frozen decoderDmatD_{\mathrm{mat}}convertsZ0Z_{0}into surface PBR materials, lit from the left and right.
Figure 2:Qualitative comparison with given geometry. Enlarged crops compare reference-view details; novel views show the completed appearance.
Figure 3:Comparison with commercial systems: each row shows the input and reference-view/back-view renderings from commercial systems and SUPRA-Tex.

Figure 4:Native observation encoding with GT geometry and materials. (a) Partial-versus-complete latent differences across valid Complex-Tex objects. (b) Decoded albedo for three cases selected by latent-difference percentile, with shared GT-selected crops. PSNR covers all retained observed GT voxels, not only the displayed crops.

Figure 5:Limitations under imperfect inputs and incomplete observations.
(a) The front output exhibits local motif distortion around the dragon head; the oblique view reveals a spurious protrusion in the underlying geometry.
(b) Two front-oblique views show spurious protrusions in the upstream geometry that remain visible after texture refinement.
(c) The glossy painted-wood appearance is assigned a high metallic value. Without material ground truth, this example illustrates ambiguity in single-image material inference rather than a verified estimation error. Grayscale maps range from black (0) to white (1).
(d) Observed and unobserved base-color views show a loss of motif precision on the hidden side; boxes identify the enlarged details.
The front output in (a) and both outputs in (d) use unlit base color; the oblique output in (a) and both outputs in (b) use PBR rendering under the same neutral lighting.

Figure 7:Examples from DTC-Tex and Complex-Tex.Ten selected assets from DTC-Tex (top) and Complex-Tex (bottom), shown in their designated reference views. Examples include dense text, fine patterns, and reflective surfaces.

Figure 8:Dark bias on unseen surfaces with zero-filled observations.The calculator and dish are shown with their input images, followed by shaded and albedo renderings from the zero-filled model and SUPRA-Tex. The zero-filled results darken the unseen surfaces; SUPRA-Tex retains the corresponding green and red-and-white materials. Each comparison uses the same geometry and perspective view.
Figure 10:Reference-view appearance during early training.Renderings correspond to the experiment in Fig.9; our model recovers the reference colors and floral patterns within 300 steps.
Figure 11:Twelve given-geometry comparisons. Novel views show the completed appearance.

Figure 12:Qualitative comparison of end-to-end single-image asset generation (Table3) across four cases. All methods use the same reference image. Pixal3D⋆and SUPRA-Tex share predicted geometry; other baselines use their own geometry pipelines. For each object we show the input, the reference-view rendering, and a novel view. Reference views assess text and repeated patterns; novel views assess the continuity of the completed appearance.

Figure 13:Single-view generation, two-view fusion, and back-view editing. The first condition panel shows the input photograph (upper left) and generated front (lower right); other panels show designed back-view materials.

Figure 14:Additional comparisons with commercial models across eight cases. Each row shows the input image and front/back renderings from Hunyuan3D, Rodin, Tripo, Meshy, Hi3D, and SUPRA-Tex. Model versions and evaluation settings are given in AppendixC.4.
